summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of mechanical aortic valve replacement, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, coronary artery disease, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for acute onset epigastric tightness and shortness of breath. Evaluation revealed volume overload with pulmonary edema, which resolved after hemodialysis. Cardiac workup showed no evidence of acute myocardial infarction, and symptoms were attributed to acute on chronic decompensated diastolic heart failure. Her INR was subtherapeutic on admission due to recent warfarin hold, and she was managed with heparin and warfarin reinitiation. Testing for pulmonary embolism was deferred given clinical improvement, stable condition, and contrast allergy. She improved clinically, was discharged home with services, and instructed to monitor daily weights and INR with close follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Heart valve replaced by other means
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
